label: Schabziger
note: Made only in Glarus; the green comes from blue fenugreek (Schabzigerklee, Trigonella caerulea). Grated, never sliced

about.text: Schabziger is a hard, green, strongly flavoured Swiss cheese made only in the canton of Glarus from the Ziger of skimmed milk and powdered blue fenugreek. A Glarus assembly fixed its recipe and origin stamp in 1463, one of the earliest protected brands; today one company, Geska, makes it.

how.label: ripen the Ziger, add blue fenugreek, press into cones
how.text: The sources disagree on the order and timing (Wikipedia: heat milk with fenugreek sap, acidify, curdle the whey at 90 °C, press, dry; Swiss press: long ripening of the Ziger before grinding).

steps.name: acidify
steps.note: Skim milk is acidified with lactic, citric or acetic acid.
The whey is curdled at 90 °C, giving the Ziger.
The Ziger is ripened in perforated vats or cloth bags under stones.
Ground with the blue fenugreek (Trigonella caerulea) at the grinder.
Stored 3–8 months after grinding, in the Swiss press sources.

processing.text: The Ziger is ripened 4-12 weeks (Swiss press sources), then ground with fenugreek, salted and stored; Wikipedia gives pressing 6-8 days and drying 2-6 months instead, and the sources disagree on the order.
